summary.en-US: Shorten the current page using your own service and copy its URL or title link.

description.en-US: Requires an existing Shortener service account and a dedicated create-only access token. Configure your service origin in Settings. Opening the toolbar popup sends the active page URL and title to that service to create a short link. Copy the URL or a formatted title hyperlink. No advertising, analytics, background browsing collection, or developer-operated shortening service.

privacy_policy.en-US: The active page URL and title are transmitted to the service origin you configure when you open the popup. The dedicated access token is sent only to that service for authentication. The service origin and token are stored locally, not synced. The page title is also used locally for formatted clipboard links. No telemetry is sent to the extension developer. Your chosen service controls its own link storage and retention. Forget settings removes local credentials but does not revoke the token or delete server-side links.

version.approval_notes:
Shortener Companion 0.1.0 is a client for a self-hosted service, not a developer-operated shortening service. No hosted demo or shared login/token is supplied. Reviewers can create their own isolated local instance and account as follows.

SERVER SETUP (separate from add-on rebuild): the attached extension source archive does not contain the server. Public server source and README: https://github.com/lucination/shortener/tree/783feaa68db35792e3b4b3570f73c4ee56a67113 . On a native amd64 or arm64 machine with Git, OpenSSL and Docker with Compose, use a new directory and free local ports 3000/8025:

git clone https://github.com/lucination/shortener.git shortener-review
cd shortener-review
git checkout --detach 783feaa68db35792e3b4b3570f73c4ee56a67113
export ADMIN_TOKEN="$(openssl rand -hex 32)"
export ANALYTICS_SECRET="$(openssl rand -hex 32)"
docker compose config --quiet
docker compose run --build --service-ports --rm -e SMTP_SECURITY=plain app

Before running the foreground app command, retain ADMIN_TOKEN locally (for example, inspect it with printenv ADMIN_TOKEN in that same terminal). Keep this terminal running after the image build finishes. This command starts Mailpit as a dependency and explicitly allows plaintext SMTP only on the isolated local Compose network; the pinned Compose file otherwise lacks SMTP_SECURITY for its non-loopback mailpit hostname. Do not use this local POC as a public deployment recipe. Configuration was validated, but this server build/start was not runtime-tested for this submission preparation.

ACCOUNT: Open http://localhost:3000/_/ in desktop Firefox, sign in with the ADMIN_TOKEN generated and retained above, choose Users -> Add user, enter an address you choose in Email address and press Confirm. No personal or deliverable email address is required: all mail stays in local Mailpit. Open http://localhost:3000/, enter that same address in Email and press Send sign-in link. Open http://localhost:8025, find the captured message and open its sign-in link in the same Firefox profile. No passkey enrollment is required.

TOKEN: In the signed-in workspace open Account -> Access tokens. Set Token name to Firefox review, retain the default expiry (90 days), press Create access token and Copy token. Save the one-time value before leaving Account. This is a dedicated create-only token, not the administrator token or a session cookie.

EXTENSION: Install the submitted add-on in desktop Firefox 140 or newer and accept Firefox's declared data-transmission consent (browsing activity, website content/page title, authentication information/access token). Open the add-on's Settings (also available through about:addons -> Shortener Companion -> Preferences). Enter http://localhost:3000 in Service URL and your newly issued token in Access token; press Save and allow the requested localhost host permission. HTTP is accepted only for loopback; non-local installations require an HTTPS origin without a path. Credentials are local, not synced.

REVIEW: Open an ordinary HTTP(S) page (not about:, an AMO page or another protected Firefox page) and invoke the toolbar action. Opening the popup sends that page's URL/title with the token only to the configured service via POST /api/links and creates one link. It attempts to copy the short URL automatically; if denied, press Copy URL. Click the page title in the popup to copy a formatted HTML hyperlink with URL-only plaintext; it does not navigate. Copy Markdown is a separate explicit plaintext action; native Markdown MIME is optional and capability-dependent. Copy retries within this popup do not create more links; closing/reopening the popup creates another. The link should appear in the service's Links workspace. After any uncertain request outcome check Links before reopening. This local Compose configuration returns short addresses with hostname localhost and no port; add :3000 manually if testing redirection locally. This does not affect creating or copying the returned address.

CLEANUP: Forget settings removes local credentials and the host grant, but does not revoke the token or delete server links. Use Account -> Access tokens -> Revoke for the review token. Stop the foreground app with Ctrl-C, then run docker compose down in the review directory (do not add -v; SQLite data is retained).

ADD-ON SOURCE: TypeScript sources, exact dependency lock and deterministic build instructions are attached; see extension/FIREFOX-PUBLICATION.md, Reproduce from source. Rebuilding the add-on does not need Rust, Docker or service credentials. The full server checkout above is separate. Desktop Firefox acceptance is separate from Android support; Android runtime/UI has not been verified. Lucide icons retain their bundled ISC/Feather notices.
